Activity.description:
The tool calls a native entry makes and the results it reports.
One provider message can carry several of each.

AgentConnection.description: How far an agent can use Mash, judged from its user settings.

oneOf.description: No usable Mash MCP registration: the agent cannot reach Mash.

The Mash MCP tools are registered and usable; the plugin (history
skill and session hooks) or another part needs attention.
Expected, with nothing needing attention.

roots.description: The configured locations, or the ones found on this machine.

expected.description: The machine has this agent's data or CLI, so an integration is expected.

Answer.description:
A tool's answer as an agent receives it: the structured reply and the text
beside it. `failed` covers tool errors and rejected arguments alike.

allowed_roots.description: Only explicit provider attachment references within these roots can be retained.

BaselineCoverage.description: Baseline coverage for one node, read from the transfer catalog.

effective_at.description: When the choice/claim applied, in Unix milliseconds; unknown stays null.

recorded_by.description: Attribution supplied by the caller, not authenticated human identity.

services.description: Targets not listed here are machines.

Catalogue.description: What the server publishes about itself: the same listing an agent reads.

first_message_id.description:
The chat's first message by display position, which `view` accepts.
None when the chat has no retained messages.

matches.description: Up to three distinct matching excerpts, ordered by relevance.

copies.description: Other indexed copies of this evidence, usable as view anchors.

projection_span.description: Primary message's search projection; excludes display ellipses.

missing.description: Parts of an expected integration that are not installed.

next_action.description: What would repair this agent, or null when nothing needs attention.

oneOf.description: The local Qdrant search service that indexing and every search use.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments as a JSON object; absent means none.

absence_proven.description: False: scan success and retained rows do not prove complete provider history.

after.description: Inclusive message timestamp in Unix seconds.

before.description: Exclusive message timestamp in Unix seconds.

DashboardCatalog.description: A bounded catalogue, retaining machine identity even for copied histories.

DecidedBy.description:
Who made a decision. An agent may settle a choice of its own, such as how
to structure code, by citing the message where it made and explained it.

decided_by.description: Omit for the person's decision; `agent` for a choice the agent made.

elapsed_ms.description: Core time includes configuration and model admission, excludes CLI startup.

filter_fields.description: Requested predicate names, not values, Boolean structure or removal counts.

selected_artifacts.description: Selection is policy, not a claim about candidate counts or inference calls.

shared_vector_override.description: Requested shared override, not a claim that remote retrieval completed.

local_below.description:
Batches with fewer new texts than this use the local model, so a
routine refresh does not wait for a remote worker to start. Zero
sends every batch to the worker.

oneOf.description: Caller asserts this is the person's endorsement, not an injected report.

Failure.description: What a failed request answers with, whatever the route.

Field.description: Predicate names only; diagnostics never echo filter values or the query.

FingerprintReport.description:
Duplicate-history report across the group, keyed by canonical chat
fingerprint. Fingerprints are content hashes; no plaintext is exposed.

duplicate_vector_bytes.description:
Approximate duplicated vector storage in Qdrant (f32 per message at the
group's embedding width). Text and index overhead are excluded.

duplicated_chats.description:
Chat identifiers that appear with the same fingerprint in more
than one node.

redundant_copies.description: Extra copies beyond the first, per duplicated chat.

redundant_messages.description: Messages carried by those redundant copies.

baseline.description: Most recent progressive baseline for the node, if one was started.

unpublished_nodes.description:
Configured group members with no retained publication. None means the
responding service did not supply its configured membership scope.

Fusion.description: Query-only candidate fusion; independent of embedding/build identity.

recency_weight.description:
How much newer messages move up the final order, as a percentage of
relevance's weight; 0 ranks by relevance alone.

Icon.description:
A URL pointing to an icon resource or a base64-encoded data URI.

Clients that support rendering icons MUST support at least the following MIME types:
- image/png - PNG images (safe, universal compatibility)
- image/jpeg (and image/jpg) - JPEG images (safe, universal compatibility)

Clients that support rendering icons SHOULD also support:
- image/svg+xml - SVG images (scalable but requires security precautions)
- image/webp - WebP images (modern, efficient format)

mimeType.description: Optional override if the server's MIME type is missing or generic

sizes.description: Size specification, each string should be in WxH format (e.g., `\"48x48\"`, `\"96x96\"`) or `\"any\"` for scalable formats like SVG

src.description: A standard URI pointing to an icon resource

theme.description:
Optional specifier for the theme this icon is designed for
If not provided, the client should assume the icon can be used with any theme.

IconTheme.description: Icon themes supported by the MCP specification

oneOf.description: Indicates the icon is designed to be used with a light background
Indicates the icon is designed to be used with a dark background

representation_version.description: Qdrant lexical payloads and their ranked text index, with literal verification.

Managed.description: A Qdrant installed by `mash qdrant install`, as `mash status` reports it.

logs.description: Where Qdrant's own output goes: a file, or the command that shows it.

service.description: The systemd unit, launchd label or scheduled task name.

filters_before_limit.description: Placement of metadata/scope predicates, independent of call completion.

providers.description: Local scan evidence only; null when the publisher does not report it.

retained.description: Scoped canonical row counts; null when this source does not report them.

tools.description: A native entry's structured tool calls and results.

MetaObject.description: See [MCP general fields](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#general-fields) for notes on _meta usage.

redacted.description: Text is retained as a redacted UTF-8 view, never the original secret-bearing bytes.

artifacts.description: None means the service did not report artifact publication states.

instance.description: The local database that owns this node's publications.

source_silver.description: Retained source-node certificate, not the server-owned canonical revision.

backfill_since.description: Fixed setup cutoff for explicit backfill; absent uses the 3-day default.

ProjectionSpan.description: Half-open Unicode-scalar character offsets, not bytes or canonical offsets.

freshness_warnings.description: Include read-only local indexing freshness warnings with search results.

Ranking.description: Query-only ranking over the active lexical and dense candidate artifacts.

Reachability.description:
Whether the configured Qdrant process answers. This is liveness only:
collection schemas and search readiness are reported separately.

oneOf.description: A supported Qdrant answered at the configured HTTP URL.
Nothing answered: the service is stopped, missing or on another port.

Something answered but refused the request, or is not a supported
Qdrant (an API key mismatch or an old version, for example).
Not a Mash command: start the Qdrant service at the reported URL.

purpose.description: Unknown for records written before evidence provenance was retained.

RedactionSettings.description:
Where a node masks recognizable credentials, configured under `[redaction]`.
Each destination defaults on; credentials in canonical silver are never
masked (`<private>` spans never reach it: see [`private_text`]).

output.description: CLI and MCP output: search, view, chat listing and attachments.

publication.description: History uploaded to the shared server. Changing it republishes everything.

RerankerEngine.description: Where contextual reranking ran. One search pass uses one engine.

oneOf.description: The configured remote reranking worker.
The local CPU, because the configured remote worker did not answer.

RerankerFallback.description: Why a search configured for remote reranking used the local CPU.

oneOf.description: No reply within the configured bound, typically a cold worker.
The connection failed or the worker returned an HTTP error.
The reply did not match the request, recipe or score bounds.
The configured token environment variable is unset in this process.
The installed reranker differs from the worker's pinned model.
The query or candidates exceed the worker's request limits.

timeout_milliseconds.description:
How long a search waits for the worker before it reranks on the
local CPU instead. A cold worker takes far longer than this.

earliest_message_at.description: Observed message bounds in Unix milliseconds, not a completeness interval.

state.description: Completion of a recorded scan, not completeness of all historical chats.

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page of the same ranked list; null on the last page.

notice.description: Why an empty result may not mean the history lacks the subject.

ServerTarget.description: A target that is a shared server rather than a machine.

ServiceState2.description: What the supervisor reports about the installed service.

oneOf.description: The supervisor has no such service.
The supervisor gave up after it exited with an error.
The supervisor could not be asked.

ServiceStatus.description: The configured local Qdrant service, as one bounded request observed it.

installed.description: The Qdrant `mash qdrant install` set up on this machine, if any.

message.description: Why it is not reachable, and how to start it.

Settings.description: The settings, with whether this dashboard accepts changes to them.

revision.description:
Names the file's contents. A change states the contents it was made
against, so an edit made elsewhere in between is not overwritten.

shared.description: Whether a shared server is configured, so history can go to it.

Setup.description:
One machine's agent integrations for a dashboard, step by step. A peer
dashboard sends this to the one asking, so local paths are left out.

build.description: The build of the Mash binary that inspected the machine.

duplicates.description: Duplicate-history report, only when `--shared` asked for it.

local_qdrant.description:
Whether the configured local Qdrant answers, apart from schema
compatibility (`local_views_error`) and search readiness (`ready`).

next_action.description: The command that would make progress, or null when nothing is left.

detail.description:
One line on what the operation found or why it failed. These are the
fixed sentences the probe and playbooks write, never command output.

Tool.description: A tool that can be used by a model.

_meta.description: Optional additional metadata for this tool

description.description: A description of what the tool does

icons.description: Optional list of icons for the tool

inputSchema.description: A JSON Schema object defining the expected parameters for the tool

outputSchema.description: An optional JSON Schema object defining the structure of the tool's output

title.description: A human-readable title for the tool

ToolAnnotations.description:
Additional properties describing a Tool to clients.

NOTE: all properties in ToolAnnotations are **hints**.
They are not guaranteed to provide a faithful description of
tool behavior (including descriptive properties like `title`).

Clients should never make tool use decisions based on ToolAnnotations
received from untrusted servers.

destructiveHint.description:
If true, the tool may perform destructive updates to its environment.
If false, the tool performs only additive updates.

(This property is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint == false`)

Default: true
A human-readable description of the tool's purpose.

idempotentHint.description:
If true, calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments
will have no additional effect on the its environment.

(This property is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint == false`)

Default: false.

openWorldHint.description:
If true, this tool may interact with an "open world" of external
entities. If false, the tool's domain of interaction is closed.
For example, the world of a web search tool is open, whereas that
of a memory tool is not.

Default: true

readOnlyHint.description:
If true, the tool does not modify its environment.

Default: false

title.description: A human-readable title for the tool.

call_id.description: Links results to this call within the chat.

input.description:
The provider's arguments, verbatim; a JSON string when the provider
records encoded or free-form arguments.

name.description: The provider's tool name; absent only where the provider omits it.

ToolResult.description: One reported tool result. Its output stays in the entry's content.

is_error.description: Present only where the provider records an error flag.

ViewResponse.description:
Where a view's messages sit in their chat, so a short window is not
mistaken for the whole conversation.

chat_id.description: The chat the viewed message belongs to.

message_count.description: Every message the chat retains, including other branches.

notice.description: How to read on when messages before or after the window were omitted.

omitted_after.description: Messages later than the last returned message.

omitted_before.description: Messages earlier than the first returned message.
